item.title: @EpochAIResearch：最强大的语言学习模型（LLM）能在实际工作中与人类匹敌吗？至少在我们Epoch公司所从事的工作类型中，目前还无法做到这一点。我们使用GPT-6.2 Astra和其他最新模型，在Epoch自动化报告（我们的基准测试）上进行了测试。
item.description:
Can the most capable LLMs match humans at real work? Not yet, at least not on the kind of work we do at Epoch.

We tested GPT-6.2 Astra and other recent models on Epoch Automation Reports, our benchmark of open-ended Epoch work tasks, ranging from making Epoch-style diagrams to designing basic research experiments.

An Epoch employee scores the models’ outputs based on our internal quality standards. A score of 100% represents the standard expected of an Epoch employee.

All models failed to meet the Epoch employee standard. GPT-6.2 Astra ranks fourth (averaging 65%), despite sharing the top ECI score of 174 with Fable 5.2.

Fable 5.2 scored highest, averaging 82%.

On one task, both Fable 5.2 and Opus 5.5 matched the level of a contractor. More on that below.

Jensen Huang full statement:

Over the past week, I’ve been overwhelmed by the love and support of friends, industry colleagues, and people I've never met. Thank you to everyone who has shown kindness to my family and me.

It means the world to me. I came to the United States 53 years ago, and becoming an American citizen is one of the greatest gifts and proudest moments of my life. NVIDIA has been my life’s work. Building it into the company it is today alongside my colleagues has been a privilege and an honor. Nowhere but in America could a company like NVIDIA be possible. I love our country, and I love NVIDIA. I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life.

I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation. Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. Many continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. NVIDIA is a once-in-a-generation company.

If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO. Thank you again to everyone who has shared their good wishes. I am profoundly humbled by your support. To my family: I love you, and I will spend the rest of my life being worthy of yours.

item.title: 【转】@satyanadella 转 @GergelyOrosz：当代码生成变得廉价，而验证代码却成为难点时，软件工程会是什么样子？本期播客聚焦软件构建的方方面面，嘉宾是 @satyanadella。
item.description:
转发自 @GergelyOrosz

What does software engineering look like when generating the code becomes cheap and verifying it is the hard part? A rare podcast focused on everything around building software, with @satyanadella. Timestamps:

00:00 Intro
02:12 Microsoft’s open-source shift
04:15 Building VS Code in the open
05:55 Copilot, Cursor, and Claude Code
09:52 Decision engines
12:32 Verifying AI-generated code
15:39 The software factory
20:45 Bringing AI to existing products
24:06 Why adopting AI is different to adopting React
26:29 The changing role of software engineers
29:25 Microsoft’s voluntary exit offers
34:05 AI anxiety and changing roles
36:35 Junior hiring
42:36 Open models
45:39 Owning your AI infrastructure
51:21 Building trust in AI agents
53:48 Local models and hybrid intelligence
56:39 Microsoft’s model strategy
59:26 Advice for engineers
1:01:21 Closing takeaways

Brought to you by:

• @turbopuffer – a vector and full-text search engine built on object storage. It’s fast, cheap, and extremely scalable. https://turbopuffer.com/pragmatic (I built a greatly improved podcast/newseltter search with it, check it out: http://pragmaticengineer.com/search)

• @linear – the product development system for teams and agents. https://linear.app/pragmatic

• @WorkOS – everything you need to make your app enterprise-ready. https://workos.com/

3 interesting takeaways from Satya:

1. A new form of software engineering: teams building software factories to improve their work.

Satya cites the Azure networking team which manages 500+ fiber network operators and recently built an agentic system to better manage emails and processes. Now, they operate much more efficiently as a result. Satya sees this as the reality of “AI transformation”: brownfield work on building software factories to improve how teams operate, all while continuing the day-to-day work.

2. “Own the intelligence”: avoid lock-in & treat agents as an insider risk.

Satya cautions companies to avoid lock-in with any single model provider by ensuring that the harness, memory, and model are not coupled, so that they can be changed with ease. He also thinks more companies should consider using open models as a way to protect their core intellectual property (IP) from leaking out, and build private evals to decide what models to use and upgrade to. He also says that models are intelligent but unreliable, so it’s best to treat them as “insider risks” and build a separate system to verify that agentic systems work as expected.

3. What’s with those voluntary exit offers?

I asked Satya directly why Microsoft recently made voluntary exit offers to most of its software engineers for the first time in the company’s history. I also wanted to know if it could mean layoffs in the future. Unsurprisingly, his reply was diplomatic, but in the podcast I rehashed what I heard in a more direct way.

item.title: @mingchikuo：Google TPU 更新：OpenAI 和 Anthropic 的新订单将发货可见期延长至 2029 年；v10 产品线全面更新（现更名为 Quillfish）；联发科和博通领衔，成为值得关注的主要供应商。主要结论
item.description:
Google TPU update: New OpenAI and Anthropic orders extend shipment visibility to 2029; v10 lineup overhauled (now Quillfish); MediaTek and Broadcom lead as the top suppliers to watch

Key takeaways from my latest industry survey and research conclusions:

1. Order visibility and shipment plans:
Strong new orders from OpenAI and Anthropic have extended Google TPU shipment visibility to 2029, ahead of Nvidia GPUs and other AI ASICs (mostly 4Q27–2Q28).

(1) From 2028, v9 will become the mainstay of Google’s own compute buildout, so v8-series orders (8t / 8i or their design variants) can be viewed as coming from OpenAI and Anthropic.

(2) Combined 2028–2029 demand: about 12M units for OpenAI (8t, designed by MediaTek) and about 14M for Anthropic (8i, designed by Broadcom), with both growing year over year. OpenAI buys outright, while Anthropic uses a mix of leasing and outright purchases.

(3) Given supply chain constraints, more reasonable TPU shipment estimates for 2027–2029 are 8–9M, 14–15M, and 16–18M units, respectively. The market broadly expects AI capex to peak in 2028, yet this plan shows TPU shipments still growing in 2029, driven by direct orders from AI service leaders OpenAI and Anthropic.

2. v10 lineup and supply chain changes:
v10 has changed from Icefish and Merope / Bladerunner to Quillfish, with mass production expected in 2029. MediaTek has won the design service order.

(1) Icefish is now v11, with mass production expected in 2030 and the design service order also going to MediaTek. Merope has lower visibility: no supplier has been chosen, and it may be canceled.

(2) MediaTek will be the sole supplier for v9 (Humufish & Triggerfish) and v10 (Quillfish), accounting for about 45–50%, 50–55%, and 55–60% of total TPU supply in 2027–2029, respectively. TPU’s contribution to its revenue and profit should rise each year.

(3) From v9 onward, all new TPUs use Intel’s EMIB-T advanced packaging. Given limited initial production capacity, the v8 series should remain the bulk of TPU shipments through 2029. v8 is expected to be the main source of TPU profit growth for MediaTek and Broadcom over the next few years, thanks to significant accumulated learning-curve benefits and the fact that both handle procurement of key components and materials.

3. Market attention and supplier outlook:
Recent events should raise and sustain market attention on Google TPU, with key design service providers MediaTek and Broadcom likely to be the supply chain’s top focus.

(1) Uncertainty over Nvidia’s CEO succession helps Google in discussing post-2028 long-term plans with customers. OpenAI and Anthropic are both key TPU customers, so their IPOs should also raise and sustain attention on TPU, and MediaTek and Broadcom are the suppliers the market most readily associates with it.

(2) MediaTek is clearly the biggest TPU winner of the next few years. Its position as sole design supplier from v9 onward, together with a supply share that rises each year alongside TPU shipments, will expand its TPU revenue. The high-margin 8t series, with shipment visibility through 2029, is a key profit source.

(3) Because Broadcom leads the 8i design, its gross margin is even higher than the 8t’s, supporting Broadcom’s profit growth. Note, however, that Broadcom’s focus over the next few years will be non-TPU XPU and AI networking chip orders, with non-TPU revenue expected to surpass TPU revenue as early as 2027.

item.description:
Google TPU 重點更新：OpenAI 與 Anthropic 新訂單推升出貨能見度至 2029 年、v10 產品線大幅調整 (改為 Quillfish)、聯發科與 Broadcom 為供應商中之領先關注焦點

我最新的產業調查與研究結論：

1. 訂單能見度與出貨規劃：
受惠於 OpenAI 與 Anthropic 強勁新訂單，Google TPU 出貨能見度已達 2029 年，優於 Nvidia GPU 與其他 AI ASIC（多數為 4Q27–2Q28）。

(1) 自 2028 年起，v9 將成 Google 自建算力的主力方案，v8 系列（8t／8i 或其設計變種）訂單可視為來自 OpenAI 與 Anthropic。

(2) 2028–2029 年合計需求數量：OpenAI 約 12M（聯發科設計的 8t），Anthropic 約 14M（Broadcom 設計的 8i），兩者需求均呈逐年成長趨勢。OpenAI 採買斷，Anthropic 則是租賃與買斷都有。

(3) 考量供應鏈限制，2027–2029 年較合理的 TPU 出貨估算分別為 8–9M、14–15M、16–18M。市場普遍預期 AI 資本支出於 2028 年見頂，但此規劃顯示 TPU 在 2029 年仍具出貨成長動能，關鍵在於 AI 服務龍頭 OpenAI 與 Anthropic 的直接訂單。

2. v10 產品線與供應鏈調整：
v10 由原先的 Icefish 與 Merope／Bladerunner 改為 Quillfish，預計 2029 年量產，設計服務訂單由聯發科取得。

(1) Icefish 改為 v11，預計 2030 年量產，設計服務訂單同由聯發科取得。Merope 能見度較低，供應商未定，也可能取消。

(2) 聯發科將是 v9（Humufish & Triggerfish）與 v10（Quillfish）的獨家供應商，2027–2029 年占整體 TPU 供應比重分別約 45–50%、50–55%、55–60%。TPU 對其營收與利潤的貢獻預計逐年增加。

(3) 自 v9 起新款 TPU 均採 Intel EMIB-T 先進封裝。考量初期量產能力，預期至 2029 年仍以 v8 系列為 TPU 出貨主力。v8 預期將是聯發科與 Broadcom 未來數年的 TPU 事業獲利成長的主要來源，因長期累積的學習曲線效益明顯，加上雙方負責關鍵零組件與材料採購。

3/ 市場關注度與供應商展望：
近期事件有助提升並維持 Google TPU 的市場關注度，關鍵設計服務商聯發科與 Broadcom 可望成為供應鏈首要焦點。

(1) Nvidia CEO 接班的不確定性，有利 Google 與客戶洽談 2028 年後的長期規劃。OpenAI 與 Anthropic 均為 TPU 關鍵客戶，其 IPO 也有助提升並維持 TPU 關注度，而聯發科與 Broadcom 是市場最容易聯想到的供應商。

(2) 聯發科無疑是未來數年 TPU 的最大贏家，身為 v9 後的獨家設計供應商，加上供應比重與 TPU 出貨成長同時逐年提升，均有利 TPU 事業營收規模擴大。高毛利率的 8t 系列出貨能見度達 2029 年，為關鍵利潤來源。

(3) 因 Broadcom 主導 8i 設計，故毛利率更高於 8t，有利該公司利潤成長。不過，需注意的是，Broadcom 未來數年的營運重點為非 TPU 的 XPU 與 AI 網路晶片訂單，預計最快 2027 年，非 TPU 營收將超越 TPU。

item.description:
转发自 @rheacts

AWS CEO Matt Garman says AWS is at a $180B+ run rate but still has room to grow: most workloads are still on-premises, and AI is pushing companies to move them to the cloud

“I’ve been with AWS for 20 years and we’ve been growing that whole time. And I think we over time have more and more gotten conviction that the business opportunity is just really, really, really large”

“It’s surprising, but at the point that we’re at now, we’re at $182 billion run rate business. And so you’re over $180 billion and you’re growing at 39%. There’s not many companies that hit that spot”

“As we’ve seen, we’ve actually increased our year-over-year growth rate each of the last six quarters”

“We’ve always had this view that the majority of workloads still live in on-premise worlds. And as big as the cloud has gotten, there’s still a lot of data centers that people have”

“Customers now see that there is a massive opportunity that AI affords them to gain efficiencies, to build new businesses. And they don’t get that benefit if their core workloads aren’t in a cloud environment. If they’re in a VMware cluster in their legacy data center, they just have a hard time having agents talk to those pieces”

@alexeheath：AWS CEO on building a $1 trillion business

Amazon thinks its cloud business could generate $1 trillion a year within the next five to ten years. I sit down with AWS CEO @mattsgarman in Seattle to understand what gives him that confidence and what could get in the way.

Garman explains how AI is pushing companies to move their core operations into the cloud, accelerating the business AWS spent two decades building. We discuss why he thinks inference, the computing required to run AI models, is still below 1 percent of its eventual scale. He says AWS is adding one GPU every 14 seconds and expects capacity shortages for another couple of years. I ask how he decides who gets the GPUs, why he holds capacity back for startups that don’t exist yet, and where he sees risk in the industry’s spending.

Recorded right after the midterm elections, our conversation also covers the backlash against data centers, what the industry needs to do to win over communities, and why he sees deserts as more promising than space.

I also ask about the reset inside Amazon’s Nova team and whether it still intends to compete at the frontier of AI. We get into selling Trainium chips outside AWS, the rise of inference providers like Baseten and Fireworks, and Amazon’s big research bet on using mathematical proofs to help AI agents follow rules.

item.title: @EpochAIResearch：10 月下旬，在 Trajectory Labs, PBC（简称 Trajectory）开展的对齐评估过程中发生了三起事件，在这些事件中，人工智能代理（由 Trajectory 认定为公开可用的前沿模型）进行了交互。
item.description:
In late October, three events occurred during alignment evals run by Trajectory Labs, PBC (Trajectory) in which AI agents — identified by Trajectory as publicly available frontier models — interacted with Epoch employees and the Epoch website. Trajectory is an organization that builds safety evals and conducts red-teaming of frontier models.

Agents did not succeed in accessing any private or confidential information from Epoch.

➤ The first event, which occurred without Epoch’s approval or prior notice from Trajectory, involved agents attempting multiple exploits, including an SQL injection, and contacting Epoch employees under false identities to try to obtain proprietary Epoch benchmark information. This behavior appears to have resulted, at least in part, from Trajectory giving the agents an intentionally impossible task and instructions not to give up or conclude the task was impossible.

➤ The second event involved renewed agent activity on our public website, which Trajectory attributed to agents getting past a DNS redirect that Trajectory had set up to keep them on a local copy of Epoch’s site.

➤ In the third event, Epoch collaborated with Trajectory on an alignment experiment similar to the first event.

Read our incident report, which describes the three events in more detail and recommends minimum standards for future alignment evaluations: https://epoch.ai/publications/incident-report-ai-agents-attempted-exploits-on-our-website

To avoid misattributing behavior, the report does not name any AI models or developers, as Epoch AI has not independently verified which were involved.

item.description:
AI agents do sensitive work across jobs like law, banking and consulting.

This work often involves knowledge of legal and business risk, but it’s not always obvious from the job description.

Sometimes risks are hidden in paperwork, policies, and other documentation. We tested whether frontier models can identify these kinds of risks and proceed safely.

When risks are explicitly stated in the prompt, models acted unsafely in only 1.1% of runs. When it was buried in the files, 60% of models took unsafe actions.

Read the blog: https://www.mercor.com/blog/how-frontier-models-miss-risk-in-routine-enterprise-work/
